title: Side Remarks: Por Cierto, A Propósito and Dicho Sea de Paso

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *por cierto* and *volviendo a lo que decíamos* from B2 Unit 28, with *a propósito (de)* and *dicho sea de paso*: phrases that mark a side remark and the way back. They are for speaking and talks. Imagine you are telling a friend about the Chaco: you want to add a detail, and then return to your point.

sections.title: Side remarks and the way back
rows: El Chaco tiene pocos habitantes; por cierto, ¿has visto el mapa?
*por cierto*: by the way (a new thought)
A propósito de los menonitas, llegaron al Chaco en 1927.
El quebracho, dicho sea de paso, tiene mucho tanino.
*dicho sea de paso*: incidentally, between commas
Volviendo a lo que decíamos, el Chaco es una región muy seca.
*volviendo a lo que decíamos*: back to the main line

items.spanish: El Chaco tiene pocos habitantes; por cierto, ¿has visto el mapa?
items.english: The Chaco has few inhabitants; by the way, have you seen the map?

items.spanish: A propósito de los menonitas, llegaron al Chaco en 1927.
items.english: Speaking of the Mennonites, they arrived in the Chaco in 1927.

items.spanish: El quebracho, dicho sea de paso, tiene mucho tanino.
items.english: The quebracho, incidentally, has a lot of tannin.

items.spanish: Volviendo a lo que decíamos, el Chaco es una región muy seca.
items.english: Going back to what we were saying, the Chaco is a very dry region.

sections.content: A side remark is short and you should come back to the main line afterwards. To add a main point, use *además* (A2 Unit 28), not these phrases. *A propósito* alone means "by the way"; *a propósito de* needs a noun.
